While thousands of companies claim to sell #AI agents, only a fraction are actually building real ones.

The test is dead simple: look at what the product actually outputs:

- If it’s a classification (spam or not spam), a number, or a probability, it’s not generative AI.
- If the output is new text, images, or video that didn’t exist before, it is.

Google’s own products show this perfectly:

1. Gmail’s spam filter relies on classification, so it’s NOT generative AI.
2. Google Docs’ “Help me write” generates brand-new text from scratch, which IS generative AI.

3 (more) common #AI terms most people don’t know:

Term 1: Grounding.
Without it, AI answers from memory, which may or may not be correct. Hand it the actual document and say “answer from this,” and now the response is grounded in something real. Whenever accuracy matters, give the AI something to reference.

Term 2: RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation).

linkedin.headline: Writer & Entrepreneur. I write The Saturday Essay for 200,000+ ambitious people living and working on their own terms.
linkedin.about:
For more than a decade, I lived the kind of life ambitious people are told to want. I helped build two companies past $1B in valuation and raised more than $300M in venture capital. By 33, I was Chief Revenue Officer at a venture-backed company, making more money than I’d ever imagined. And quietly falling apart.

I was burned out, anxious, drinking too much, and increasingly convinced that if I kept going, I might not see fifty.
Then one afternoon, in our house in Los Angeles, I had a panic attack so severe I ended up on the kitchen floor.

My wife, Jennifer, called 911. The paramedics came. And by the time they were standing in our home, it was impossible to keep pretending this was just stress.

When it passed, I knew that the life I was building wasn’t the one I wanted to live.

So Jennifer and I quit our high-paying jobs with almost no plan. We bought a house in the mountains of Upstate New York, drove across the country, and started our lives over.

In the years since, I’ve built a $15M one-person business with no employees and no investors, and an audience of 1.5M+ people has followed along. But that’s not the real story.

The real story is that I got my life back, slowly, unglamorously, one difficult choice at a time.

Today, I spend that life writing.

Every Saturday, I publish one essay about the choices that made it possible: leaving the obvious path, redefining ambition, using money for freedom instead of performance, and building something of your own without letting it consume you.

These are the choices that can look wrong from the outside and still be right for the life you actually want.

If that’s the kind of conversation you’ve been wanting to have with yourself, I’d love to have you with us.

posts.caption:
If you chase after money, it has a funny way of avoiding you.

At least, that's what I've found in my career.

Instead, I'd much rather focus on something better:

Big, painful, miserable problems.

I started learning how to solve these problems back in 2009 in my startup days, and quickly figured out how valuable that was.

Solve one painful problem? Here's some money.
Solve another one? Here's more.
Keep solving them? Here's a boatload.

When you can save people money or time (or both) AND help them sleep better at night, you have incredible earning potential.

So work on that skill…

The worst thing in the world is getting fired without a backup plan.

I've watched it happen to so many good people.

$200,000 take-home pay one day.
$0 the next day.

What a nightmare.

That's why planning for the worst, while working hard to prevent it, is a great 1-2 punch.

Here's what I'd recommend:

1. Make some noise

Get online daily and share how you think about your industry. Let people see your name and face and become synonymous with something.

2. Build a network

Once you've made a little noise, jump into DMs. Invite people to connect. Grab coffee. Meet on Zoom. Help people.…

Successful people work on things that bring them joy and keep them interested.

Sure, they may do a few things that suck here and there.

But it's rare.

Take my business, for example:

- I write about what I love
- I help customers that I can benefit
- I deliver products that improve lives
- I have conversations with interesting people

All of that stuff is exciting and fun.

None of it fills me with dread, so a Monday isn't all that different than a Saturday.

So, when you're building your business, here are a few helpful questions to ask yourself:

1. What's a business I could run for…

The problem with loyalty to a company is that it often doesn't go both ways.

So, be sure you're not working yourself to death.

Don't let work cause you to miss dinners, skip workouts, not see your family, or miss out on that vacation.

None of that stuff proves you're “committed to the mission."

And it's more important to be committed to yourself and your family.

Work hard.
Care deeply.
Do excellent work.

But don't devote your life to your work.

Your job should support your life, not the other way around.

I know a lot of folks feel like they have to do this, because they lack…

If you want to be great at something, surround yourself with the best people.

This is why I hate most “move somewhere cheap and peaceful” advice.

It's good for 45-year-olds like me, but it's terrible for young ambitious people.

But I get it. Cheap rent's awesome.

Being the smartest guy or gal in your zip code isn't.

If you’re young and you're serious about getting insanely good at something, go where the competition scares the hell out of you.

Surround yourself with folks who are:

Making more money than you.
Building and shipping faster than you.
Taking bigger moonshots than you…

If you want to build an incredible life, hang around incredible people.

That doesn't necessarily mean rich and successful people.

Kind people.
Interesting people.
People who lift you up.
People who normalize some form of excellence.

I've had such a wonderful time building an eclectic collection of friends.

Some are my health-nut friends, or intellectual friends, or athlete friends, or business friends.

Everyone has something interesting that they bring to the table.

A huge mistake I see people making is that they surround themselves with people who bring them down.

Complainers,…

One of the best business hacks is being your own biggest cheerleader.

Trust me, you're going to need it.

When you're just starting out, very few people will believe in you.

Maybe your spouse.
Maybe your friends.
Maybe your family.

Maybe.

So you better believe in yourself enough for all of them.

Talk confidently.
Toot your own horn.
Wear your own merch.
Celebrate the wins nobody else cares about.

You might feel a little ridiculous.

Good.

Because one day, if things work out, something funny happens:

Everyone who doubted you suddenly remembers being incredibly supportive.

"I always…

A business that requires you all day, every day, is my personal nightmare.

I see so many entrepreneurs bragging about freedom while glued to a Slack channel, taking calls on vacation, and checking email at 5 a.m.

That’s the opposite of freedom.

A good business should make your life easier as it gets better.

More control over your time.
More money not attached to hours.
More time to be around your family.
Freedom to decide what your week looks like.

That requires some discipline.

Because growth almost always gives you a reason to add complexity.

Another hire.
Another offer.
Another…

Your 20s are probably the worst time to optimize for comfort.

You have fewer obligations, more energy, and a longer runway than you’ll probably ever have again.

Don't spend those years trying to make your life cushy.

Easy job.
Easy schedule.
Easy coworkers.
Easy expectations.

Too many people do, then they hit 35 and wonder why nobody trusts them to do something difficult.

Do the opposite.

Find people who are better than you and make yourself useful to them.

Take on some work that scares you a little.

Become the person who can be trusted with expensive, painful problems.

And then…

Most entrepreneurs try to build a business first and then cram their life around it.

I think that's a mistake.

Before you build anything, you should decide what your business is going to make possible in your life.

Here are some important questions to think through:

How many hours do you want to work?
How much income is actually enough?
Do you want weekends protected?
Do you want employees?
Do you want meetings?
Do you want to travel?

Those answers should help shape the business model that you eventually choose.

Because the answers affect what you sell, how you price it, how much…

If you're great at what you do, but nobody knows, that's a "you" problem.

The market isn't going to discover you because you deserve it.

But, of course, someone half as talented is posting their work, explaining what they know, showing results, asking for the business, and getting paid.

Being uncomfortable with self-promotion is expensive.

But you don't need to become obnoxious.

You do need to get good at three things:

1. Show your work.

Talk about what you're building, what you're learning, what worked, and what failed. Be open, honest, and helpful.

2. Make your value extremely…

The 24/7 grinders won't experience the joy of a relaxed weekend with their spouse.

What a tragedy.

What's the point of doing all of this work if you never get the joy of downtime?

"Rise and grind."
"I'll sleep when I'm dead."

Lol. OK.

There's nothing wrong with hard work. I love working hard.

And there's nothing wrong with the occasional all-nighter or tough week, or workaholic month.

I get that. I've been there, too.

But if your identity is that work always gets 100% of your time, you're going to be a very sad and lonely person as you age.

If I could give one piece of advice to any…

5 money rules my wife and I follow as a couple aged 45 with two kids.

1. We don’t spend money to look rich.

We spend to become wealthy and gain freedom of our time.

So, there’s no car. It’s rented.
We own the house we live in, no other real estate.

No spending on brands. No spending just to show off to people.

2. We spend extravagantly on high-quality food.

We know that what goes into our body is ultimately the biggest wealth we have, and unfortunately, healthy food is not cheap.

3. We spend on experiences more than things.

Things give you happiness once, and they have no end.

You…

Before you say yes to marriage, check these 5 things.

1. Why are you getting married? Is it for the sake of society? Is it for the sake of your parents? Is it for your own good?

2. How do you handle fights with your partner? Because fights will continue. If you handle them properly, then relationships will progress.

3. Do you have an alignment on money and responsibility? How will you spend money? How will you share responsibilities?

4. Do you have space for your own personality? You can make friends without involving their friends. You can live your own life without depending on…

We overcomplicate self-improvement.

We wait for the big change, the perfect plan, the dramatic turnaround.

But most of life gets better through small rules, followed again and again.

Wait 30 days.
Do the 2-minute task now.
Never shrink yourself for a relationship.

Start with one this week.

4 signs that your life is much better than you think.

1/ Someone in your family has stopped worrying about you - because they trust you now.

2/ Your 18-year-old self wouldn't believe where you've reached.

3/ People now ask you for advice about something you once used to panic about.

4/ One bad day doesn't ruin your entire week, one bad week doesn't ruin your month, and one bad month doesn't ruin your year.

Sometimes, you've already made more progress than you realise.

There's a difference we often miss.

Being dependent means you need them to function.
Being dependable means they can count on you, and you on them, without either of you losing yourselves.

One comes from fear.
The other comes from strength.

The strongest relationships aren't two people who can't live without each other.

They're two whole people who choose, every day, to be someone the other can rely on.

But by the time we reached 40, we already knew we’re going to stay here. That’s why we chose this place.

2/ At that time, we had enough money that we could afford its EMI and its down payment for the house we wanted to live in.

Should you tell your parents how much you earn?

There’s a case for yes. They raised you, supported you, and may have every reason to know.

But there’s another side.

Once they know your salary, expectations can change - a bigger house, a car, a trip, a higher contribution at home.

So instead of telling them exactly how much you earn, you could tell them what your money can do for them.

“I can contribute ₹X towards the house.”

“I can afford this trip.”

“I can cover this EMI.”

Tell them what your money can do, not necessarily how much you make.

A counterpoint of view - do you agree?

Some people don't add to your life.
They slowly drain it.

The ones who confuse you.
The ones who hurt you and call it a joke.
The ones who take your energy and give nothing back.

We keep them around out of guilt, or history, or habit.

But protecting your peace isn't cold.
It's necessary.

You're allowed to walk away from anyone who only knows how to take.

5 questions people ask - and how we hear them.

1/ “When are you getting married?”

We hear that nothing I’ve done in life so far means nothing until I get married.

2/ “How much do you earn now?”

We hear that my entire worth is based on one salary, one number, and that will give me a rank.

3/ “Sharma ji’s son, well…”

We hear that I will never be enough. Someone else will always be doing better than me.

4/ “You studied so much and you’re doing this?”

We hear that if I make my own choices in life, that will never be accepted.

5/ “You’ve gotten a little healthy.”

When a child is punished for the truth, they don’t stop doing the thing.

They just get better at hiding it.

Fear doesn’t build honesty.
It builds distance.
It teaches a child that the safest option is to never let you see who they really are.

The kids who grow up telling their parents the truth aren’t the ones who were scared into it.They’re the ones who knew the truth was safe.

We all want 3 things: to be understood, chosen and loved ❤️

Conversation expert @vvanedwards says great conversations are one of the fastest ways to get there.

Whether it’s with your boss, your partner or someone you’ve just met, deeper conversations can help you skip the small talk and feel genuinely understood.

What’s the best conversation you’ve had recently?

Never Ever Say “Nice To Meet You” | @jenniferhudsonshow

Loved this quote by @jennifer.garner on @aspirewithemmagrede

I know I’ve found the smallest of kind gestures to make the biggest impact.

A thoughtful text. Holding the door. Checking in on someone. Letting someone merge in traffic. Complimenting a stranger. Remembering the little thing someone mentioned weeks ago.

You never really know what someone is carrying, and a tiny gesture that takes you five seconds might be the thing that makes their entire day a little lighter.

Be the reason someone leaves an interaction feeling a little more loved than they did before. 🤍

What’s a small act…

Quick question: what do you think successful people do that the rest of us don’t?

The usual guesses are grit, a 5 a.m. alarm, or some genius-level IQ.

What I saw up close was a lot smaller than that, and a lot easier to copy. Three of the patterns are about how they think. Two are about how they treat people, especially the people who can’t do anything for them.

And every one is small enough to try in your very next conversation.

I’ll share the research behind each one. (Including the one that didn’t hold up. Yes, I’ll tell you which.)

Your pre-order of Conversation is your ticket in.…

posts.caption:
Hi, I’m Hala 👋🏼 and if you think I’m just another case of overnight success…

You’re missing the real story.

Because it took me 8 YEARS (and counting) to get where I am today.

Once upon a time, there was a version of me who had:
👎🏼 No audience
👎🏼 No business
👎🏼 No proof things would work.

Just a vision of what I wanted to achieve and the drive to get it done.

I started recording podcast episodes as a side hustle…
While working a full-time job…
And I ended up building something bigger than I ever even imagined.

When I look back at my life, it’s easy to package it all into a…

When they asked how much he'd sell for, he threw out a crazy number.

$5 billion.

They laughed. The biggest brand in the industry — Grey Goose — sold for $2.2 billion.

"You want more than twice that? Never gonna happen."

He shrugged. "I don't want to sell it anyway."

Others approached. He said no. Kept building.

Then Bacardi came back. $5.1 billion.

He said yes immediately.

Not because he was desperate. Because he knew his number. He knew his worth. And he waited until someone else saw it too.

Most people undersell because they're afraid to name a big number. They negotiate against…

If Elon Musk was standing in an elevator with you right now, what would you say? 👀

Most people would freeze, stumble or word vomit their entire life story in 10 seconds.

This week I sat down with bestselling author, TV host, and pitch expert Forbes Riley (@forbes_riley), and she broke down the real-life pitch that landed her on Grant Cardone's 10X stage.

Forbes was in a Vegas hallway. Grant was at the other end with his entire entourage. She had no meeting. No introduction. Just 20 seconds and a strategy.

She didn't approach Grant. She approached Elena.

And 30 seconds. That's all it…

Not saying your phone is spying on you…

But if your LinkedIn posts are getting crickets, consider this your sign 👀

I’m hosting a free training on all things LinkedIn growth!

⏰ Join us Oct 15 @ 1pm ET

👉🏼 What’s changed and what’s working on LinkedIn

👉🏼 Build a profile that gets you noticed

👉🏼 Create content that builds trust

👉🏼 Turn engagement into clients and opportunities

👉🏼 Build your 30-day LinkedIn growth plan

👉🏼 Live Q&A with Hala

Comment “WEBINAR” and I’ll send you an invite.

That instant “spark” you feel with someone might NOT mean you’re compatible. 👀

Sometimes, it means they feel familiar.

This week on YAP, I sat down with attachment expert Adam Lane Smith (@attachmentadam) to unpack the relationship patterns most of us don’t realize we’re repeating.

We talked about why chemistry can pull you toward the wrong people, why expecting your partner to read your mind creates resentment and what secure couples do differently when conflict gets messy.

One of my biggest takeaways?

A healthy relationship isn’t one where you never fight, get triggered or mess…

The old American dream is dead. Waiting until you are 65 to start living your life is a trap.

This week on YAP, I sat down with financial expert Haley Sacks (@dowjones) to talk about why our generation is redefining success and walking away from the 40-year corporate grind.

Our parents were taught to stay locked into a desk, collect a pension, and hope for freedom decades later. But corporations are not loyal to you, and trading four decades of your life for a finish line at 65 makes zero sense.

I learned this firsthand when I walked away from corporate to build YAP. Real security comes…

Jacqueline had put $150,000 of her sales savings into Howdy. Then COVID paused the orders, with her son due in May and the company’s money going toward keeping the business afloat.

On YAP, I sat down with Howdy founder Jacqueline Samira (@jac_samira) to talk about a founder’s crisis point.

When her baby shower was cancelled, she asked friends and family to send the gifts because she had nothing for the baby and no money to buy it. Then the business changed direction: companies saw that remote work could work, and customers who had paused their orders came back. Howdy began taking off in…

I used to record a podcast episode and post... once. 😅

Now? One episode turns into a full week of content in under 20 minutes.

This is how I stay consistent without recording every single day.

But here’s my take: repurposing isn’t about doing less work. It’s about making one great conversation work harder for you.

Which prompt are you trying first?

I shared with Gary Vee why I thought my Instagram was underperforming compared to my LinkedIn and YouTube.

I had an old account, algorithm “baggage,” being shadow-banned before, being Palestinian.

He didn’t let me finish before shutting it down. ❌

He told me ➡️You’re not good enough yet.

That one stung. But he was right.

Here’s the advice he gave me, with no sugarcoating:

📵 Stop blaming your algorithm.
Whatever excuse you’re reaching for (an old account, wrong platform, bad timing), it’s rarely the real issue. It’s almost always the content.

📈 Quantity is not debatable.
You either…

Stop asking which choice is easier. Ask which hard is worth it. 🤷🏻‍♀️

Leaving corporate was hard.

But staying in a career I knew wasn’t meant for me would've been harder.

Starting YAP with no guarantee it would work was hard.

But never finding out what I was capable of would've been harder.

The same applies to your health, relationships, career, money and dreams.

🏋🏻‍♀️ Discipline is hard. Regret is harder.
🚀 Starting is hard. Wondering “what if?” is harder.
🫶🏼 Starting over is hard. Staying somewhere you’ve outgrown is harder.
🎯 Betting on yourself is hard. Waiting for…

A surprising tax case explains why everyday clothes are harder to claim.

On YAP, I sat down with financial educator and Mrs. Dow Jones creator, Haley Sacks (@mrsdowjones), to talk about the unusual costume deduction case and ordinary creator clothing.

I asked whether an influencer can deduct clothes worn on camera. Haley answered with the unusual Chesty Love tax case: the court accepted a business rationale for an exotic dancer’s implants because they functioned as part of her performance costume.

Haley then turns back to an ordinary influencer dress. If the person can wear it to dinner,…

To everyone who's ever asked, "How are you managing it all?"

Respectfully… I'm managing today. 😂

We'll deal with tomorrow tomorrow. 🤷🏻‍♀️

The guy inside just told you you'd be back. They always come back. He said it kind, which somehow made it worse.

ㅤ
You're shaking your head like you don't. You're doing the face. You do it well, you've had practice.
ㅤ

Hello my friend! There are a lot of new folks here on the ’gram and I thought I would (re)introduce myself.

I’ve been doing this content thing since 2017. That’s pretty old in content years. We didn’t say “content” or “creator” then—I just wanted to make a living as a writer. And at the time, I thought that looked like sending emails to strangers from MailChimp! 😂

As I tried to deconstruct how people were making a full-time living sending emails, I started writing about what I was learning. People liked that. So I kept explaining what I was learning as I went along.

Fast forward a few…

⚡️Comment INBOX to join my newsletter and get posts like this every Sunday.

I just closed the books on year eight as a creator, and, in many ways, it was the best year yet!

I share this graph each year because it highlights a few important truths:

1.) I’ve been doing this for eight years
2.) It took me four years to have my first 6-figure year
3.) My revenue actually dropped in year three
4.) You can see how powerful compounding is

Along this eight-year journey, most of my peers have quit. A lot of them were talented and even found success! But this path is hard – and if I would’ve quit…

posts.caption:
Reintroducing myself here, as this past year has been filled with exciting new projects that I’m thrilled to share! 🥰👏🏼

Did you know about all of them? Let me know what surprises you!

This video is an act of self love.

I wasn’t even going to share it. I created it for myself, for Noah and Adam…

But I decided to post it, as an invitation for you to capture more of the things that bring you joy.

Because when you do, you will realize the love that surrounds you. And that your life is already good enough.

PS: despite of how “perfect” my life may seem on that video, what I didn’t capture was the many tears that were shed, the fear, the uncertainty and the disbelief we experienced and continue to experience with the current geopolitical climate.

Still, we did our best to…

Recently, I was invited to speak at this amazing conference, and @melrobbins was a speaker there too!

So, I posted an Instagram Story mentioning Mel, and when she saw it… SHE WROTE BACK!

I went from excitement 🤩 to shock 🤯 to horror 😱

“OMG, WHAT am I gonna talk about with Mel Robbins…? this is so awkward…someone make it STOP.”

My first impulse was to NOT answer her message, it was to act as if nothing had happened, and then say: “ohhh nooo…, I JUST saw this, tomorrow I have to deliver 3 speeches, I don’t think we’ll be able to meet, I travel in the afternoon. Maybe next time?”

But,…

Thank you, PULSE Network, for trusting me with your audience here in Arizona! ♥️

Grateful for @keppleroncampus for the partnership on this one! To many more successful events together 🫶🏼
Change is not risky anymore.

Only one thing I would change 😳

Remember to take a photo together next time!!! I still can’t believe we forgot about that 🤣

Never mistake silence for disengagement.

Last month I faced one of those quiet crowds, and I won't lie, it was a bit uncomfortable from start to finish. But then, one after another, people came up to share how deeply the talk had moved them.

A quiet crowd doesn't mean they're not paying attention. It means they're taking notes.

When has silence taught you more than applause ever could?

I feel so privileged to have this career, to speak in rooms like these, and to surround myself with these people 🥹♥️🙏🏼

It makes all the hard work, sweat, and tears feel so worth it.

Thank you @youtube @google for having me 🙏🏼 It means the world to me to share my story with you.
Hey Austin! I'm ready for you!!! Can't wait for tomorrow 🥰🥰🥰
My favorite personal story about imposter syndrome 🫣

Reframing this question will take you to places you never imagined possible for you 🙏🏼

Can’t wait to see you on stage

MichellePoler.com 🫶🏼

Putting this carousel together was honestly fascinating 🤯.

It forced me to look back and realize how much has changed over the years.

Not just my actions, but my mindset. My beliefs. The stories I used to tell myself.

I highly recommend doing this exercise, even if you never post it.

Sometimes the best way to see how far you’ve come is to compare who you are today with who you used to be.

Now I’m curious… which slide surprised you the most?

If there’s one thing humanity has ever truly agreed on, it’s this:
We all want to be happy.
We want to make those we love happy.
And we all want to love and be loved.

These three truths could guide not just us, but the future we’re building with AI.

If our technology learns from our best qualities, not our fears, it could help us create a world rooted in compassion, happiness, and love.

Because maybe the real upgrade we need… is in our humanity.

#MoGawdat #AI #EthicalAI #FutureOfHumanity

In the moments when we make decisions, whether in business, money, or life, our emotions are always louder than the facts. But the truth is simple: data sees what our feelings hide.

You don’t need to predict the future. You don’t need to guess better. You just need systems that keep you grounded, consistent, and rational when your mind wants to rush.

Let information guide your decisions. Let discipline replace emotion. And let intelligence, human and artificial, work with you, not against you.

The world rewards clarity, not noise.

#MoGawdat #AI #DecisionMaking #Wisdom #FutureThinking

Suffering is not a glitch. It's built into the design.

But that's never been the argument against happiness. The argument for it is much smaller and much more honest, you can move the dial. Not too perfect. Not too permanent. Just slightly further from where you are now.

From minus one to minus point five is still a choice. And a choice means you're not a passenger.

Start there. Pick one thing, a skill to learn, a thought to reframe, one person or place that makes the weight a little lighter. You don't need a transformation. You need a direction.

Two years without a salary.

Millions stolen by people considered family.

Ten moments of complete giving up.

And on the other side of all of that a clarity about purpose and calling that could not have come any other way.

Some seasons do not break you.

They just burn away everything that was never meant to last.

Boxer went from boardroom joke to standalone listed entity outperforming its former parent company.

In retail. In South Africa. During one of the most difficult consumer environments in recent memory.

The strategy was not complicated.

Go where the value-focused consumer is and execute better than anyone else in that space.

They did exactly that. And the market rewarded it.

The South African consumer has been under sustained pressure for a long time.

Elevated costs. Sticky inflation. High rates. Weak job creation.

Each layer compounds the one before it.

The businesses that survive this environment will not be the ones that waited for conditions to improve.

They will be the ones that understood the pressure, adapted to it and built for the consumer that actually exists right now.

The most powerful differentiator in business right now is not technology or branding or social media presence.

It is being so complete and so convenient that leaving becomes the inconvenient option.

ShopRite figured that out.

The question is what industry you are in and how you apply the same thinking to it.

posts.caption: VEGAS, Baby! 💍 || The plan WAS, go to the GRAMMY’s with my two times Grammy Considered fiancée, @hello_azureantoinette. That WAS the plan. Then in true poetic fashion, VEGAS. Sorry kids! Sorry mum and dad! Surprise! We eloped! We got married!! I’m so happy and floating on cloud nine. Thanks to my wife @hello_azureantoinette who organised the entire thing. A few days ago she says “Let’s get married in Vegas - just get a dress babe and show up.” I bought three dresses online, one of them fit, two got sent back and it was all beyond perfect. Thank you to our dear friend @smiledarlingphotos for…

In case anyone apart from my mum is interested in this, I have a new website. Boom! Go check it out at emmaisaacs.com and HUGE thanks to the dynamic duo @hello_azureantoinette and @jordanne.co who designed it together. Dream team. They didn’t even ask me one question and just got it done and nailed it. Thank you @hello_azureantoinette for the brand design and thank you for always making me laugh in awkward photo shoots that I loathe 😂😂

Here are some memories, some pieces of joy, and lots of fun masking as work. Such a privilege to host my magnificent love @hello_azureantoinette and her Show + Tell event last night at the @businesschicks HQ and catch up with beautiful friends who feel like family. Little Louis even made a brief cameo! Thanks to our incredible team for all their love and hard work and to @smiledarlingphotos for capturing the moments we never want to miss.

Too many moments a day, I look at you and think, “Why do you stay?”

Like… what happened? Did you lose a bet? Was there a clerical error? Did someone accidentally tick the wrong box on the cosmic paperwork?

There isn’t another human on the planet with the fortitude, determination, loyalty, resilience and love you show me, our six babies, and three furry freeloaders.

You catch me every time I fall, pep-talk me back into believing (in anything), and keep me laughing an unreasonable number of times a day.

It’s your birthday today, and although I regularly curse God for sending me SUCH A…

We all need women to look up to, to aspire to, to believe in. Every time we got to bask in @gloriasteinem’s wisdom, we were better for the experience. She was gracious, unfathomed, interested, ours. There are few women who stand for women, truly. It’s easier to seek fault, criticise, make yourself feel better by belittling others. Gloria would never stand for that. She knew and espoused the brilliance of women, the disparity, the lies told … She was truth and she was unwavering. She made sense. She made us believe our power was possible and more than that, that it was deserved. Rest well…

Some pictures are the quiet proof that hope is worth holding onto.

Watching these six hilarious, incredible humans grow has been both the greatest challenge and the greatest privilege of my life. There were many times I wasn’t convinced a moment like this would come, which makes these photos all the more precious. I’m so grateful we captured this season together.

To my beautiful wife @hello_azureantoinette, thank you for always knowing what I need before I do. Most thoughtful gift ever (of course).

And to @mfortphoto (and my bestie @lady_may) - I’m still in shock at how effortless you…

If your love language is words, marry a poet. Teach them patience and grace. Watch them soften and stretch right before your eyes. Hold their dreams and doubts with sincerity, and most importantly, do the work of seeing the world through their lens.

Fight well and shorter each time. Be the first to forgive. Say thank you as often as memory allows. Let them go to Bunnings and JB Hi-Fi as much as they’d like.

I call Azure my Friday night, because time spent with her feels like the best part of every week. She makes me laugh, and endures me laughing at my own jokes too many times a day. Yes,…
Survived my last first day of big school drop-off! Go get ‘em Louis! You make us all soooo proud!

Only two weeks until my book launch in Sydney! Let me know if you are coming!

@businesschicks is hosting the event on August 11. Appropriately titled - Blood, Sweat and Tears – an evening of laughing, learning and lifting the lid on perimenopause.

The hilarious @hello_azureantoinette will be onstage with me so expect real talk, evidence based advice AND a healthy dose of inappropriate humour.

Members and non-members are welcome.

So grab your besties, your sister, your work wife, and come for a night of big laughs, big truths and even bigger hot flushes.

🎟 Tickets:…
A beautiful night in Bel Air with this hottie @hello_azureantoinette and @roxanegay74 Thanks for the 📸 @toekneero

Last day to win a pair of these amazing @sonyaustralia WH-1000XM5 headphones in my favourite colour, smoky pink. I’ve popped the link in my bio and all you need to do is tell us which woman inspires you in 25 words or less. There’ll be three lucky winners, so get at it!!!

linkedin.about:
Ich bin Unternehmerin, Co-Gründerin des FC Viktoria Berlin und seit Dezember 2023 Vorstandsvorsitzende des Startup-Verbands.

Was mich ausmacht ist unternehmerische Leidenschaft, ein hohes Maß an wirtschaftlichem und gesellschaftspolitischen Verantwortungsbewusstsein und die Freude daran, mich aktiv für die Zukunftsfähigkeit des Wirtschaftsstandorts Deutschland einzusetzen.
Im Juli 2022 habe ich zusammen mit 5 Co-Gründerinnen die Frauenmannschaft des FC Viktoria Berlin übernommen. Unser Ziel ist es, die Mannschaft innerhalb von 5 Jahren von der Regionalliga in die 1. Bundesliga zu führen und den Frauen-Fußball in Deutschland nachhaltig zu verändern und nach vorne zu bringen.

Kindern chancengleichen Zugang zu digitaler Bildung zu ermöglichen ist in meinen Augen eine der Kernvoraussetzungen für die Zukunftsfähigkeit unseres Landes. Dafür habe ich 2017 den Digitale Bildung für Alle e.V. gegründet.

2020 habe ich mein Buch „Das Neue Land“ veröffentlicht und wurde dafür von der Frankfurter Buchmesse mit dem Sonderpreis „Unternehmerbuch des Jahres“ ausgezeichnet. In unserem wöchentlichen Podcast „FAST & CURIOUS“ spreche ich mit meiner Co-Host Lea-Sophie Cramer über Unternehmertum, Gründen und unseren Blick auf die Wirtschaft.

Was machen die Volksparteien falsch? Auf Social Media begegnen junge Menschen, nur AfD und Linke. Und wenn die früheren Volksparteien Talente haben, die anders kommunizieren, dann haben die es oft schwer, in der Partei aufzusteigen. Mit der Unternehmerin und Investorin @verenapausder habe ich genau darüber im @politico @berlinplaybook_podcast gesprochen: Was muss sich ändern, damit nicht nur die Ränder stärker werden? Wo muss @bundeskanzler seine Politik ändern, wo müssen aber auch Strukturen und Wahlrecht verändert werden. Und zum Schluss ein positiver Ausblick: Wo steht Deutschland…

DEIN ERNST, DEUTSCHE BILDUNGSPOLITIK? 🤯

Die neuen PISA-Zahlen sind da - In Deutschland verfehlt inzwischen rund ein Drittel der 15-Jährigen das Mindestniveau in Mathematik und Lesen.
Das sind nicht einfach nur Zahlen in einer internationalen Vergleichsstudie, sondern dahinter stehen junge Menschen, die Schwierigkeiten haben, Texte zu verstehen, Informationen einzuordnen, mathematische Alltagsprobleme zu lösen oder wissenschaftliche Zusammenhänge zu beurteilen.

Und noch etwas zeigt PISA sehr deutlich: Bildungschancen hängen in Deutschland weiterhin viel zu stark von der sozialen Herkunft…

Wir sind wieder da! 🎙️

Nach sechs Wochen Sommerpause sind @leasophiecramer und ich zurück - mit wöchentlich neuen Folgen @fastandcurious.pod.

In unserer heutigen Folge teilen wir Gedanken und Erkenntnisse, die wir über den Sommer hatten und die uns während unserer Podcastpause beschäftigt haben, u.a.:

- Welche Entwicklungen uns Sorgen machen: von fehlenden Zielbildern in der Politik bis zur Frage, ob künstliche Intelligenz uns geistig zu bequem macht
- Wie wir auf unsere Familien schauen, von mehr Eigenverantwortung für unsere Kinder bis hin zu einem versöhnlicheren Blick auf unsere…

🌟Meine Top-Tipps für Portugal 🌟
Weil ich immer wieder nach Portugal-Tipps gefragt werde, kommen hier meine persönlichen Highlights:

1. Galapinhos Beach: Einer meiner Lieblingsstrände! Schon die Anfahrt ist atemberaubend! Das Wasser ist glasklar, die kleine Bucht wunderschön und der Naturpark Arrábida rundherum eine große Empfehlung.
2. @nuua_beach: Super schöner Ort am Strand von Caparica mit Surfschule direkt daneben. Hier kann den ganzen Tag verbringen, ins Meer springen, frischen Fisch essen und abends bei einem @whynotsoda den Sonnenuntergang genießen.
3. @bardopeixemeco :…

✨ FITNESS UND HEALTH CHECKUP 🚀

Heute war ich in der @years_co Klinik zu meinem jährlichen Fitness- und Gesundheits-Checkup!

Es war so halb schlau den Checkup direkt nach meinem Party-Wochenende auf Mallorca zu machen, aber ich habe mich erstaunlich gut geschlagen 💪🏼 Von Hör- und Sehtest, über großes Blutbild, Lungenfunktionstest, VO2-Max und EKG bis hin zu Körperanalyse, Organ- und Gefäß-Ultraschall und Mobilitätstest war alles dabei! Und dann durfte ich sogar noch Versuchskaninchen vom neuen Gehirntest sein, der deine kognitiven Fähigkeiten und den Alter deines Gehirns misst 👍 Nachdem…

💖 Fiesta de la Vida auf Mallorca dieses Wochenende 💖

Mit so viel Licht, Liebe und Sonne im Herzen geht es jetzt zurück nach Berlin! Ab morgen beginnt wieder der Alltag und das ganz normale Leben und die Bilder, Farben und Gefühle dieses Sommers werden noch lange nachwirken ✨

♥️ WIEDER VEREINT ♥️

Diese Woche machen @leasophiecramer und ich 2 Tage @fastandcurious.pod Strategie-Workshop und nächste Woche kommen wir aus unserer Sommerpause zurück und freuen uns schon sehr auf die erste Folge nach den Ferien 💥☀️It is good to be back!

posts.caption:
3am thought → messy notes app → Word doc → 1,000 airports.

Nobody tells you the origin story looks like that.

No glamorous advance. No publishing plan. Just a half-finished idea and a baby on my hip.

Make it exist first. Make it good later.

What’s living in your notes app?

Congratulations to the Class of 2026 🎓

I had the honor of speaking at commencement this weekend, and while everyone is talking about AI, automation, and what the future will look like, I wanted to leave graduates with one thing they could count on:

Being a good human always wins.

Technology will change. Industries will change. The jobs that exist today may look completely different tomorrow.

But kindness, integrity, curiosity, generosity, and treating people well? Those never go out of style.

Thank you to Cannon School for inviting me to be part of such a special day. And…

Hot take: we do not have the same 24 hours in a day.

The secret to my success isn’t a 5am routine or an AI prompt.

It’s a village I was privileged enough to afford.

And until every woman has access to that kind of support (affordable childcare, paid leave, equal pay) we’re asking people to run a race with weights on.

I’m proud of how far I’ve come. I’m also honest about the runway I had.

Both things are true.

The problem isn’t that women don’t work hard enough. The problem is we built a world where the village costs too much and then we call it a personal failing when she can’t afford…

Women are not responsible for managing men’s thoughts, feelings, or self-control.

We have enough reps to do already. 🙄

Here’s what I learned from the 🐐 @justbobbidotcom at @livelong_media 👉

I met her when I was an intern at the TODAY show and she was SO nice to me (not the norm for celebs + interns 😅). Turns out, she’s met so many people through just chance encounters that have changed her trajectory. So treat everyone like your future depends on it!

Bobbi started @jonesroadbeauty after her 25 YEAR non compete ended. You can be proud of what you’ve built and still want to do something else.

Jordan is the host of The Jordan Harbinger Show, where he interviews leading entrepreneurs, celebrities, creators and experts on psychology, performance, life and success. For all his work in the field, Forbes named Jordan one of the 50 best relationship-builders in the world, and Inc. Magazine recently called him “the Larry King of Podcasting.”

Jordan has shared his ideas around the world as a speaker and consultant. His work has been presented in Silicon Valley (at companies such as Google, Apple, Twitter, and Square) and to various government branches and agencies (including all branches of the U.S. Military, the Department of State, and Department of Defense). He has also given talks on security, social-engineering and psychology to BlackHat, DEFCON and Harvard Business School, and has advised private companies and law-enforcement agencies on their security and communications.

A former U.S. State Department employee and Wall Street attorney who speaks five languages, Jordan has spent several years abroad in Europe and the developing world, including South America, Eastern Europe, the Balkans and the Middle East. He has worked for various governments and NGOs overseas, traveled through war zones, led several trips through North Korea, and been kidnapped—twice. (The only reason he’s still alive and kicking is because of his ability to talk his way into (and out of) just about any situation.)

On The Jordan Harbinger Show, Jordan shares all of this experience—and the system born as a result—with his listeners.

Not because of Inception, Interstellar, or Oppenheimer.

Nolan uses the Plot Map Technique to visualize his storyline.

Writing on the internet helped me earn my first $40k as a ghostwriter.

And in less than 2 years, I scaled my ghostwriting agency to $2 million.

Want to kickstart your ghostwriting journey?

I wrote a free, 5-day email course to help you get started.

Comment "PIXAR" and I'll send it to you!

How To Audit Your Goals As A Writer

Distraction mode:
→ Chasing every "exciting" opportunity
→ Setting goals you don't actually care about
→ Feeling busy but moving nowhere

Execution mode:
→ Identifying your true priority
→ Auditing your progress every 6 months
→ Ignoring everything that isn't the main thing

The faster you level up, the more your "shiny objects" fall off a cliff. Stop distracting yourself from the one thing you actually need to do.

Why You Should Stop Building Two Businesses At Once

The confused creator:
→ Offers 4+ different subscription tiers
→ Forces readers to read a novel to understand the pricing
→ Tries to build a newsletter and a community at the same time
→ Sees stagnant growth across both ventures

The professional business owner:
→ Simplifies the offer to a clear, binary choice
→ Treats the high-end tier as a separate business entirely
→ Focuses on scaling one model to $100k+ first
→ Doubles down on what works until it’s standing

Pick one business model. Table the other. If you try to build both, neither…

Stop Writing Your Book All At Once

The biggest mistake writers make is trying to stare down a blank page and force a "whole book" into existence at once. That is a recipe for writer's block. Instead, stop trying to write a masterpiece and start assembling sections. Treat your chapters like containers—fill them one by one, remove the headers at the end, and watch the story click into place. Writing isn't about conjuring magic; it’s about breaking a massive, daunting task into small, manageable pieces that eventually connect to form something whole.

How To Start A Ghostwriting Side Hustle In 3 Steps

Starting a ghostwriting side hustle isn't as complicated as most people make it out to be.

You don't need years of experience. You just need to leverage what you already know and package it as a high-value service.

Here are the 3 steps to launching your ghostwriting business:
→ Identify your information advantage. Target clients in an industry where you already possess specialized knowledge that the average person doesn't have.
→ Offer 1 of the "Big 3" services. Focus on social ghostwriting, educational email courses, or newsletter…

Why Your Digital Products Fail To Deliver Outcomes

Most digital product creators fail because they confuse "help" with "outcome."

They promise to make their reader "successful" or "happy." But those are subjective goals. You cannot measure them. You cannot deliver on them. And your reader will never know if they actually achieved them.

If you want to build a product that people actually pay for, you have to reverse engineer the process:
→ Define where your reader is today (their starting point)
→ Identify the specific, tangible transformation they need
→ Create objective metrics to…

How To Get Verified Purchases On Your Book Launch

The most effective way to gain momentum on launch day isn't a massive ad budget—it’s social proof. Amazon’s algorithm prioritizes “Verified Purchase” reviews, so you need to mobilize your inner circle immediately.
→ Ask 10–20 friends or family to buy the book
→ Ask them to leave an honest review on Amazon
→ Offer to reimburse them for the cost of the book
→ Watch as they leave a "Verified Purchase" review

The "Why" is simple: Nobody ever actually asks for the money back. They just want to support your success. People are happy to help; you…

The Hardest Part Of Building A Writing Career

5 mistakes that keep writers from succeeding at the start:
→ Believing successful creators were given an audience at sign-up
→ Treating "writing tactics" as the only thing that matters
→ Quitting because you got 11 views instead of 11,000
→ Trying to master your psychology in isolation
→ Expecting 10-year results after 10 minutes of work

Building a career isn't just about hard skills like copywriting or email marketing—it’s about the soft skill of showing up when it’s hard. That’s why community and accountability aren't luxuries; they are the…

How To Monetize Your Social Media Attention

Most creators make the mistake of sending social media traffic to a website with too many options.

If you want to move from generating attention to generating revenue, here is why your ecosystem needs to change:
→ Websites have too many distractions (About Me, Projects, Blog, etc.)
→ Too many clicks lead to lower conversion rates
→ Email lists allow you to own your audience directly
→ Newsletters turn passive readers into active customers
→ You control the channel, not the algorithm

Stop hoping people find their way around your website. Start…

Why Writing Is A Lottery Game

Stop trying to engineer your personal brand to perfection.
→ Experiment with topics outside your niche
→ Document your experiences and travels
→ Analyze which posts spark unexpected conversations
→ Double down on what you actually enjoy talking about

The goal isn't to know exactly what will happen—the goal is to take action so you can gather the data. If you don't write, you deprive yourself of the very learning experience that reveals your next big opportunity.

Since 2010, I've written regularly for the Harvard Business Review, and I’m the author of multiple books on strategy, professional reinvention, and long-term thinking — including The Long Game (WSJ & USA Today bestseller), Stand Out (named Inc.'s #1 book of the year); Reinventing You, and Entrepreneurial You.

For more than a decade, I taught executive education for Duke University's Fuqua School of Business and Columbia Business School, and have also taught at business schools around the world including IE Business School (Spain), HEC-Paris, Fundação Dom Cabral (Brazil), and more. I also hosted a weekly interview show for Newsweek for three years.

I’ve been named one of the Top 50 Business Thinkers in the World 4x times by Thinkers50; one of the Top 50 leadership experts by Inc. magazine; the #1 Communication Coach in the World by the Marshall Goldsmith Leading Global Coaches Awards; and cited by The New York Times as an “expert at self-reinvention and helping others make changes in their lives.”

Earlier in my career, I worked as a journalist, a presidential campaign spokesperson, and a producer of a Grammy-winning jazz album — experiences that continue to shape my perspective on influence, narrative, and credibility. I also write musical theater.

If you’re thinking about how to amplify your impact and get your ideas heard more widely, I’ve created a free Recognized Expert® self-assessment: https://dorieclark.com/toolkit/

posts.caption:
Hi and welcome! I’m so glad you’re here..

A big thanks to @phillipvn for the Recognized Expert photo!

RIP Dolly. She was a legend and an inspiration. Dolly had a trick to handle people who talk down to you - and you can steal it the next time someone’s patronizing to you. In this iconic 1978 interview with Barbara Walters, considered one of the toughest interviewers in the world, Dolly responds to Barbara’s questions about her appearance (‘you don’t have to look like that’) and whether she’s actually a hillbilly. Watch to see how Dolly handles it with grace and class. I taught communication at Duke for 10+ years and Dolly aced this. Follow me for more.

You don’t have to be the loudest voice in the room to stand out in a meeting. Even if you’re typically quiet or shy, this 90 second trick can help you make an impression at work. I taught communication at Duke University for 10+ years and this small technique can help. Follow me for more on building the career you want.

Here’s what to say when someone won’t take no for an answer, but you want to maintain your relationship with them. When a colleague keeps pressing, it’s easy to get irritated and snap, “I already said no” – but then you’re the one who sounds rude. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia, and this strategy can help. Follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Here’s what to say when someone gives you a backhanded compliment. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia, and here’s how to respond so you can call them out on their hidden meaning while still looking gracious. Follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Here’s what to say when someone criticizes you in front of your boss. They could have waited to tell you in private - but they didn’t. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia and here’s how to respond. Follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Here’s what to say when someone says, “That’ll never work.” It’s always easier for someone to shoot down your idea than to contribute their own – but if you argue back, you look defensive. Here’s what to do instead. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia, and this strategy can help. Follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Here’s a 9 second trick for what to say when someone tries to embarrass you in front of other people. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia, and this technique can help you respond eloquently in the moment so you don’t have to just ‘sit there and take it.’ Follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Here's how to answer 'What do you do?' when you're a stay-at-home parent. It's hard to know exactly what to say sometimes. Do you talk about the work you used to do, or what you're up to now? If you answer honestly, sometimes people might unfairly dismiss you. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia for more than a decade, and here is what to say. Follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Here's what to say when a client says, "Can I talk to your boss about that?" It's hard to refuse a direct request, but you know it will make you look bad, and your boss doesn't want the hassle. Here's a simple way to defuse the situation. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia for 10+ years, and you can follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Here's what to say when someone talks down to you. You're in a team meeting or a client presentation, or even dinner with friends, and someone decides to explain something to you that you already know...and might even know better than they do! I taught communication at Duke and Columbia for more than a decade, and here is what to say. Follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Here’s what to say when someone asks, ‘Can you actually handle this?’ It’s hard to know what to do when someone doubts you publicly, because protesting too hard only makes you look defensive. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia, and here’s what to say. Follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.

Tiffany Dufu is President of the Tory Burch Foundation, which empowers women entrepreneurs by providing access to capital, education, and community. She’s the author of the bestselling book Drop the Ball: Achieving More by Doing Less. Named to Entrepreneur's 100 Powerful Women and Fast Company’s League of Extraordinary Women, Tiffany has raised over $25 million toward the cause of women and girls. She’s the founder of The Cru, a peer coaching tech company that was acquired by Luminary in 2023. Their algorithm matches women in accountability circles to help them meet their life goals. Tiffany was a launch team member to Lean In and was Chief Leadership Officer to Levo, the fastest growing millennial women's professional network. Prior to that, she served as President of The White House Project, which trained thousands of women across the nation to run for political office.
​
Tiffany is a Trustee of Simmons University, a board member of Moms First, a member of Delta Sigma Theta, Sorority, Inc. and a Lifetime Girl Scout. She lives in New York City with her husband and two kids - but home is Seattle.

I’m excited to share that applications for the 2027 Tory Burch Fellowship are officially open.

The mission of the @toryburchfoundation is to increase women’s economic power by supporting entrepreneurs to build businesses that last. Here’s what I’m most proud of about what we’re doing and why I hope you’ll share this opportunity with a founder you know:

91% of the entrepreneurs we’ve supported over the past decade are still in business. Half of businesses fail within the first five years. And a third of our Fellows are now running multimillion-dollar…

In 2010, I had the opportunity to interview Gloria Steinem. She asked me to call her Gloria because I kept referring to her as “Ms. Steinem,” but my cultural upbringing collided with her instructions. I simply couldn’t bring myself to call an elder of her stature by her first name. I explained that, out of respect, I would need to put either “Ms.” or “Aunty” in front of Gloria.

She preferred the latter.

I’ve called her Aunty Gloria ever since.

I was introduced to Aunty Gloria by my political mother, Marie Wilson. They built the @msfoundation together, along with its other founders, and it…

Just as we were all mourning the loss of Dolly Parton, @sarabareilles gifted us with her seventh studio album, Good Grief. As if on divine cue, it’s a musical respite for any sorrowed soul. On the day of Good Grief’s release, I stayed up so late looping the tracks that, in an ironic role reversal, my teenage daughter came into my room, took my phone and headset, and told me to go to bed.

Bareilles has been on my life’s soundtrack since her 2007 hit “Love Song” topped the Billboard charts. She crosses pop, rock and country, but all I ever hear in her music is the soul. Her beautiful vocal…

We were both being honored by Women in Retail, and our photos were featured on a giant billboard in Times Square. It was drizzling as we headed outside for the group photo when Zarna turned to me and apologized for the rain.

“It’s not your fault,” I laughed.

“It definitely is,” she replied. “My mother-in-law hates me. So, on the day I get a blowout and my picture is on a billboard in Times Square, she sent the rain.”

I howled.

Later that evening, Zarna’s daughter told me her mom was a…

There are two types of people in the world: People who talk about things and people who make things happen. Entrepreneurs are the latter. I was reminded of this truth at the @toryburchfoundation’s inaugural Founders Circle. For the first time, we convened all of the Fellows we’ve supported over the past decade, including the first 2016 cohort. Being in their orbit for three days reminded me why I have so much respect for builders.

I was recently asked to name a founder and to share one quality that I admire about them. The first person I thought of was Regina Gwynn, who I’m pleased to announce has just joined the @toryburchfoundation as our Vice President of Experience.

Regina is intentional about understanding the needs of whoever she is serving. I’ve experienced this first hand as a consumer. In 2014 she Co-Founded TresseNoire, a beauty tech platform that sent traveling natural-hair stylists to your house, hotel or office. I used TresseNoire as a busy working mom to ensure my daughter felt confident about her…

I had a warning for the guests I greeted before the @toryburchfoundation’s second annual Founders Breakfast: you’re going to need Kleenex.

By the time our third honoree took the stage, the tears—and the inspiration—were flowing.
Pilar Guzmán, CEO and Founder of Half Moon Empanadas, shared a grainy photo of herself as a young girl with her late father. She told the story of walking with him through downtown Los Angeles at 15, looking up at the high-rises and declaring, “Papi, one day I’m going to work in one of those buildings.” She never imagined she would do so much more.

@guzman_pilar…

All moms have dreams for their daughters. As a Lifetime Girl Scout, one of mine involved her selling cookies. (Now that she’s touring colleges, I’ve started checking for Delta chapters—but that’s for another post.) So it meant a lot to have her by my side for a full-circle moment: being inducted into the National Board Alum Society for @girlscouts of the USA.

Girl Scouts gave me two competencies I still use every day. The first is servant leadership. Whether I’m picking up litter in a movie theater after the credits roll or executing a strategy to advance an organization, my goal is the…

My younger sister once told me, “Tiffany, you’re so boring. You never want to learn a lesson yourself.” I knew exactly what she meant. Whenever I want to accomplish something, my first move is to find someone who has already done the thing and ask for their advice. Why reinvent the wheel when I can learn from someone else’s mistakes?

The upside of this approach is that I win faster. The downside is that I don’t get as much practice failing publicly—which is how you build resilience. Still, my obsession with seeking wisdom has paid off. Over the years, I’ve collected a lot of it.

One of the…

It was a marvel to witness our team’s brilliance on the ground. Thank you Molly, Alicia, Allie and Serena for your creativity, coordination, and care. Special shout out to Haven, Jailan and Charles for your insights on our SXSW panel and for your unwavering support on my own leadership journey.

The most meaningful SXSW moment for me was breaking bread with a few of our Tory Burch Foundation…

They highlighted peer support and early belief, local community investment, institutional backing and policies like affordable childcare and elder…

Every year the @nytimes solicits readers for the best wisdom they’ve received over the past 12 months. Last week, when the list was published I immediately started pasting the most relevant quotes into our family chat:

🔅“Stop trying to calm the storm. Calm yourself, the storm will pass.”
🔅“It’ll be fine or it’ll be over.”
🔅“We tend to forget that baby steps still move us forward.”
🔅“Don’t think harder, breathe deeper. Most of us are surviving on shallow sips of air.”

Needless to say, 2025 was rough.

I’m grateful for the wins. Beyonce won Album of the Year for Cowboy Carter, we can…

I am a co-founder of Known and Built, our Fund-as-a-Service platform, where we help fund managers and innovators scale. Over the years, I've become increasingly interested in what separates BUILDERS from FLIPPERS. My recent TEDx talk expands on that idea, and why the difference is more important now than ever.

Since my book LEAPFROG: The New Revolution for Women Entrepreneurs (Penguin Random House), my writing and speaking have continued through Leap Again: No More Someday (Substack). I've advised organizations in the public and private sector including the National Institute for Reproductive Health, Hispanas Organized for Political Equality (HOPE), Vote Run Lead, WE NYC (City of New York), Launch with GS (Goldman Sachs), WOCstar Fund, the American Medical Association Health Equity Group, Accion Opportunity Fund, Connectivity Ventures (Venture Partner). I previously served on the boards of Hanky Panky and Cadence OTC.

My career began when I launched a tech startup at the age of 20. Later, I led the growth of a multinational business (30 countries) with Lionbridge (NASDAQ: LIOX) to nearly $100M in revenue, including its strategic partnership with Microsoft. And in 2012, I co-founded and taught at Entrepreneurship@Athena at Barnard College (Columbia University). In 2014, I served as interim CRO at PowerToFly, to help grow what became one of the fastest growing online hiring platforms for women in tech, and in 2019 I co-founded the trade organization for Builder Capital, an alternative asset class to venture capital.

In my former industry I advised multinationals including Disney, Microsoft, MTV, The Discovery Channel, and Mattel, as well as early-stage companies including Cranium, Seed & Spark, and TomboyX. In 2018, my first book, LEAPFROG, was named by BookAuthority as one of the Best CEO Books of All Time.

I've been included in People Magazine's most powerful Latinas, received Schneps Medias inaugural Women of Wall Street Award, and in Never Eat Alone, Keith Ferrazzi described me as a super-connector, the “fuel core of a network that makes it easy for her to tap the resources to get stuff done, and done quickly.”

Read (or see) me in places like The 4-Hour…

If you're new here, welcome, I'm Nathalie and I recently left the U.S. to return to the mountains where my ancestors are from, a dream I deferred for decades.

While a lot of things contributed to my move, it ultimately boiled down to the decision to stop pushing my joy to the proverbial "someday."

I look forward to getting to know you as I share my journey. And I hope that my - albeit imperfect - example might inspire you to Leap Again too.

Por si no nos conocemos, ¡bienvenida(o)!

Soy Nathalie, cofundadora de @scalewithKnown, y hace poco dejé mi vida en Estados Unidos para volver…

Before I turned 50, I chose to begin the process of leaving the U.S. and begin again in South America—specifically Cuenca, Ecuador, where my family roots run deep.

While I love a highlight reel, this isn't that. This was a conscious decision to prioritize mental health, physical well‑being, and proximity to the people and places that shaped me and fill me with hope.

This is a first attempt at explaining why.

I hope to chronicle the real experience of uprooting a life, returning to ancestral land, and stepping into a long‑deferred dream.

If you’re navigating your own “what’s next,” you…

linkedin.about:
When's the last time you stepped back and looked at your whole year?

Most of us move from one deadline to the next and never ask what it all adds up to.

I've been doing an annual life review for nearly two decades. For a long time, I did it wrong.

In 2013, I opened mine with the line "My diet is down the toilet." The rest of the page read like a verdict against myself. I set impossible goals, fell short, and showed up to the next review already defeated.

The process stayed about the same over the years. The mindset I brought to it changed completely.

My new book, "Life in Perspective: The Art and Power of the Annual Life Review," is the method I wish I'd had back then. It shows why starting with gratitude matters more than starting with goals, why your body knows the truth before your mind does, and why real growth happens on the scale of years, not days.

It comes out Nov. 3 in hardcover, ebook, and audiobook. (I'm also the author of "Building a Second Brain," a Wall Street Journal bestseller translated into 23 languages, and "The PARA Method.")

If you pre-order now, you get bonuses: the first two chapters right away, the recording of our Annual Review Virtual Summit, and, when you buy two or more copies, a seat in my Annual Review 2027 program for each copy (up to four), so you can bring a review buddy.

readingLog.firstImpression: From twelve posts and a LinkedIn profile, she looks like a finance veteran who now teaches and sells the idea of buying existing businesses, with a calendar of podcast recording, workshops, speaking and promotion, mostly based in Austin. Her days seem to be about deals, content and audience more than anything private, and the data is thin on friends, free time or home life, so I'd hold any picture of her weekends loosely. She is funny in a dry, blunt way, as in 'Honestly, I've always wanted a stage-five clinger', and she clearly enjoys having an opinion. A good match is probably someone who can keep up with a busy, public, work-first life, doesn't need to be the centre of her feed, and can talk about money, ownership and hard choices without treating it as a pitch.

steps.observation: The headline is 'Founder, Entrepreneur, Author' and the About leans on slogans like 'less suits, more boots' and 'Main Street over Wall Street'. It reads as a deliberate public voice, so I'll treat it as her public persona rather than a neutral CV.

evidence.quote: Founder, Entrepreneur, Author | My new book Own Or Be Owned just dropped.
My mission is less suits, more boots.

steps.looked_at: Experience entries 8 and 1, plus the middle of the arc
steps.observation: The career runs from institutional finance (Vanguard, Goldman Sachs, State Street, First Trust, with Latin America work) through a cannabis growth-equity firm to buying and growing small businesses. Contrarian Thinking, dated from December 2019, overlaps with several of the earlier roles, so the move out of the suit world looks gradual rather than a single break.

evidence.quote: ETF Consultant & Distribution Specialist @ Vanguard (2008 – 2010)
Founder - Investor @ Contrarian Thinking (Dec 2019 – Present)

steps.observation: The About says 'we value experience over degrees', yet she lists an MBA from Georgetown and a journalism and political science degree from Arizona State, plus two journalism awards. That contrast is a fair light joke for a first date, not a gotcha. The Spanish and Portuguese entries line up with the Latin America work in her history.

evidence.quote: Georgetown University (Master of Business Administration - MBA, 2011 - 2013)
We value experience over degrees.

steps.observation: The bio is 'Owner, Contrarian Thinking' followed by 'Helping you build & buy profitable businesses', and every link goes to her book or a review form. Nothing personal appears here, so the account works as a business front door.

evidence.quote: Helping you build & buy profitable businesses
http://ownerbook.com/

steps.observation: Roughly two-thirds of the twelve sell something: the book, a podcast, a masterclass or a workshop. Four posts ask people to comment a keyword to get a link or sign-up, and the rest are short lines about ownership and hard choices. Her feed is essentially her business, so most conversations with her will probably start from work.

evidence.quote: COMMENT SCALE If you’re doing five jobs and charging for one
Life is hard. Chose your hard.

steps.looked_at: Locations, guests and what's absent from the sample
steps.observation: Four posts are tagged 'at Austin, Texas' and the rest carry no location, so Austin looks like the base. She name-checks guests (Daymond John on the podcast, a Harvard talk), but across twelve posts there is no friend, family member, weekend, pet, meal or private trip. Almost everything is about work, so I'd be careful drawing conclusions about her private life from this sample.

evidence.quote: A bank once offered Daymond John a $1.3 billion credit line.
I spoke yesterday at Harvard about building businesses and how important ownership is.

Post 2 is a close-up of a book page with a boxed quote about difficulty, and post 3 is a Forbes cover with 'Buy the boring biz' on it. The profile photo is a plain grey-backdrop portrait.
